blocks.text: (I. Chron. 29)
blocks.layout: inline after incipit

blocks.text: And David blessed the Lord before the eyes of the whole assembly and David said: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of Israel, our Father from eternity to eternity, Thine, O Lord, is greatness and might, glory and victory and majesty; with regard to all in heaven and on earth, Thine O Lord, is the dominion and Thou art supreme as head of all. Wealth and honour are before Thee and Thou art ruler over all and in Thy hand is strength and might and it is in Thy hand to make all great and strong. And now, our God, we give thanks to Thee and praise Thy glorious Name.

blocks.text: seed the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizite, the Jebusite and the Girgashite. Thou didst keep Thy word, for Thou art just. Then Thou didst see the misery of our fathers in Egypt, and hear their cry at the Sea of Reeds. Thou didst provide signs and wonders against Pharaoh and all his servants and all the people of his land for Thou didst know that they had acted arrogantly against them and Thou didst gain fame for Thyself even as on this day. And the sea didst Thou divide before them and they passed through the sea on the dry land, and their pursuers didst Thou hurl into the depths, like a stone into the mighty waters.

blocks.text: And the Lord saved Israel that day from the hand of Egypt and Israel saw Egypt dead on the shore of the sea. Then Israel saw the great hand that the Lord had extended against Egypt, and the people feared the Lord and they believed in the Lord and in Moses His servant.

blocks.text: אז
blocks.layout: incipit (no citation printed)

blocks.text: Then did Moses sing together with the Children of Israel this song to the Lord and those are the words: I will sing to the Lord for He is truly exalted, the steed and its rider has He flung into the sea. My strength and song is the Lord and He was my salvation, this is my God that I may glorify Him, my father's God that I may exalt Him. The Lord is a warrior, His name is the Lord. Pharaoh's chariot and army did He throw into the sea and the finest of his captains were sunk in the Sea of Reeds. The depths cover them, they went down to the bottom like a stone. Thy right hand, O Lord, is wonderful in strength, Thy right hand O Lord shatters the enemy. And in the abundance of Thy grandeur dost Thou destroy Thy foes, when Thou sendest forth Thine anger, it consumes them like stubble. And through the breath of Thy nostrils are the waters heaped up, flowing waters stand up like a mound, the depths congeal in the heart of the sea. The enemy thought, I will pursue,

blocks.layout: top line

blocks.text: I will overtake, I will distribute spoil, my appetite will be satisfied with it, I will unsheathe my sword that my hand may deprive them. Thou didst blow with Thy wind, the sea covered them, they sank like lead in the mighty waters. Who is like Thee among the powerful, O Lord, who is like Thee so wonderful in holiness, awe-inspiring in praise, worker of wonder. When Thou didst extend Thy right hand the earth swallowed them. By Thy grace hast Thou led this people Thou hast redeemed, Thou hast led in Thy strength to Thy holy dwelling. The peoples have heard, they quake, trembling has seized the inhabitants of Philistia. Then have the rulers of Edom been terrified, as for the notables of Moab, fright seizes them, all inhabitants of Canaan have melted with fear. Let awe and dread fall upon them, through the greatness of Thine arm let them be silent as the stone until Thy people pass, O Lord, until this people whom Thou hast acquired shall pass. Thou wilt bring them and plant them upon the mount of Thine inheritance, the site for Thy dwelling which Thou hast made, O Lord, the sanctuary, O Lord, which Thy hands have established. The Lord will reign for ever and ever. The Lord will reign for ever and ever.

observations: Divine Name: 1 Chr, Neh, Ps 22:29, Obad, Zech, Deut and the Exod 15:18 repetition use abbreviated יְיָ. Exod 14:30–15:19 (except the repetition) use full יְהֹוָה, recorded with holam per the first-heh convention.
Exod 15:18 is printed twice: first יְהֹוָה ׀ … לְעֹלָם (defective, with paseq), then יְיָ … לְעוֹלָם (plene). The English also gives the line twice.
Brickwork is read right to left across each line, then down. Cells are given in each block's layout. s88 L19 has only a small gap between its cells.
Exod 15:1 starts as a full-width prose line (L13); the brickwork starts at L14.
The English Song of the Sea is set as prose and has no citation; only the Exod 14 paragraph has '(Exodus XIV. 30)'.
Neh 9:11 here has plene בִמְצוֹלוֹת, while Exod 15:5 on the same page has defective בִמְצוֹלֹת.
Psalm 150 and the ברוך verses at the top of s86/s87 are outside the requested scope and were not transcribed.
No English bands were found; s87/s89/s91 were read from the full pages.
